details:
ETERNOS SPACE: Where Missions End, Discovery Continues

ETERNOS SPACE is an interactive digital space museum developed by Henrique and Guilherme for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project was created to address an important educational challenge: how can we preserve the stories of space exploration and make scientific knowledge more accessible, engaging, and meaningful to younger generations?

Space missions may eventually end, but their discoveries, technological achievements, and scientific contributions continue to shape our understanding of the universe.

ETERNOS SPACE transforms this legacy into an immersive educational experience.

Through our platform, visitors can explore missions to the Moon, Mars, and deep space, discover the history of spacecraft, learn about scientific objectives and achievements, and understand the challenges of exploring the universe.

The platform offers interactive timelines, mission profiles, educational content, quizzes, games, and challenges that encourage visitors to actively participate in the learning process.

One of its features is METI, an AI-powered space assistant designed to help users explore astronomy and space science through natural-language conversations.

ETERNOS SPACE also includes a searchable space library, interactive activities, and personalized learning experiences with progress tracking and achievements.

Our goal is to combine reliable space science information with modern digital technology, storytelling, and gamification to inspire curiosity and make space exploration more approachable.

The project draws on NASA's publicly available scientific information and mission resources, connecting educational experiences with the real history of space exploration.

We believe that every spacecraft has a story worth remembering and that the end of a mission should never mean the end of its educational impact.

ETERNOS SPACE is more than a digital museum. It is an invitation to explore, discover, learn, and preserve the extraordinary legacy of humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Developed by Henrique and Guilherme.

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
